lines.trans: Dima, what restaurant homeless man? What are you talking about?
You see, in Moscow there are such kind traditions.
Someone sponsors an animal in the zoo, and we look after a homeless man.
Dima, do not forget that you sold the restaurant to me.
And now only I decide whom we look after.
And your job by contract is to be the face here.
Tomorrow important investors and a wife will have dinner here.
The wife is a big fan of yours, you will sit and joke with them.
Sitting and joking—that is called a corporate gig!
Dima, what is wrong with you? Did you almost cry?

examples.text: А твоё дело по контракту — здесь лицом торговать.
examples.trans: And your job by contract is to be the face here.

meanings.note: Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to trade / represent'.

examples.text: А твоё дело по контракту — здесь лицом торговать.
examples.trans: And your job by contract is to be the face here.

examples.text: Тебя посадили здесь лицом торговать, а не советы раздавать!
examples.trans: You were put here to be the face, not to hand out advice!

meanings.note: Prefix 'за-' marks beginning an action, covering, or stopping by along the way (stem 'втра').

examples.text: Об этом вы завтра поговорите с полицией.
examples.trans: You will talk about that with the police tomorrow.

examples.text: Завтра здесь будут ужинать важные инвесторы с женой.
examples.trans: Tomorrow important investors and a wife will have dinner here.

examples.text: Родион Сергеевич работает с завтрашнего дня, завтра и увидите!
examples.trans: Rodion Sergeyevich starts work tomorrow, so you will see them tomorrow!

meanings.note: Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to be; there is'.

examples.text: А может быть, лучше выпьем за нашу любовь?
examples.trans: Or maybe it is better to drink to our love?

examples.text: Ну, может быть, ты и правда очень симпатичный.
examples.trans: Well, maybe you really are very handsome.

examples.text: В этом блюде обязательно должен быть свежий базилик!
examples.trans: There must definitely be fresh basil in this dish!

meanings.note: Prefix 'у-' marks departure, removal, or successful completion (stem 'жинать'). Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to dine'.

examples.text: Завтра здесь будут ужинать важные инвесторы с женой.
examples.trans: Tomorrow important investors and a wife will have dinner here.

examples.text: Олигарх будет ужинать у нас?
examples.trans: The oligarch will dine with us?

meanings.note: Adjective formed with the common Slavic suffix '-н-' from a noun/verb root. Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('important').

examples.text: Завтра здесь будут ужинать важные инвесторы с женой.
examples.trans: Tomorrow important investors and a wife will have dinner here.

examples.text: У меня сегодня вечером важная встреча с девушкой.
examples.trans: I have an important meeting with a girl tonight.

examples.text: Не важно, я больше не хочу и не буду здесь работать!
examples.trans: It does not matter, I no longer want to and will not work here!

meanings.note: Common masculine noun meaning 'investors' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: Завтра здесь будут ужинать важные инвесторы с женой.
examples.trans: Tomorrow important investors and a wife will have dinner here.

examples.text: Вы познакомитесь со всеми нашими инвесторами.
examples.trans: You will get acquainted with all our investors.

examples.text: Крупный инвестор из Москвы приехал на встречу.
examples.trans: A major investor from Moscow arrived for the meeting.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian spatial or relational preposition meaning 'with / from', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Вот здесь можно сделать вторую летнюю веранду.
examples.trans: Right here we can build a second summer veranda.

examples.text: Мне кажется, здесь будет очень тихо и уютно.
examples.trans: It seems to me it will be very quiet and cozy here.

examples.text: Да, это факт, место здесь очень уютное.
examples.trans: Yes, that is a fact, the place here is very cozy.

meanings.note: Common feminine noun meaning 'wife' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: Как это замуж? Я не собираюсь на ней жениться!
examples.trans: What do you mean married? I am not going to marry her!

examples.text: Завтра здесь будут ужинать важные инвесторы с женой.
examples.trans: Tomorrow important investors and a wife will have dinner here.

examples.text: Жена твоя большая поклонница, посидишь с ними, пошутишь.
examples.trans: The wife is a big fan of yours, you will sit and joke with them.

meanings.note: Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('big').

examples.text: Макс, давай договоримся: ты больше никогда не будешь мне врать.
examples.trans: Max, let us make a deal: you will never lie to me again.

examples.text: Я больше не буду врать.
examples.trans: I will not lie anymore.

examples.text: Жена твоя большая поклонница, посидишь с ними, пошутишь.
examples.trans: The wife is a big fan of yours, you will sit and joke with them.

meanings.note: Prefix 'по-' forms perfective verbs or marks a brief/onset action (stem 'клонница'). Derived noun with agent/object suffix '-ник'/'-щик'/'-чик'. Common feminine noun meaning 'admirer / fan' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: Жена твоя большая поклонница, посидишь с ними, пошутишь.
examples.trans: The wife is a big fan of yours, you will sit and joke with them.

examples.text: На кухне ресторана всегда есть поклонница.
examples.trans: In the restaurant kitchen there is always admirer.

meanings.note: Prefix 'по-' forms perfective verbs or marks a brief/onset action (stem 'сидеть'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'you will sit a while', paired with 'сидеть'.

examples.text: Посиди с Викой.
examples.trans: Stay with Vika for a while.

examples.text: Давай посидим в кафе.
examples.trans: Let's sit in a café for a bit.

examples.text: Слушай, я уеду на полтора часа. Ты с Викой посиди, понял?
examples.trans: Listen, I'm going out for an hour and a half. You stay with Vika, got it?

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'them', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Понимаешь, в Москве существуют такие добрые традиции.
examples.trans: You see, in Moscow there are such kind traditions.

examples.text: Вот мой номер, позвони мне сегодня вечером.
examples.trans: Here is my number, call me tonight.

examples.text: Ну ничего, позвони мне, когда будешь один.
examples.trans: Well that is fine, call me when you are alone.

meanings.note: Prefix 'по-' forms perfective verbs or marks a brief/onset action (stem 'шутить'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'you will joke', paired with 'шутить'.

examples.text: Жена твоя большая поклонница, посидишь с ними, пошутишь.
examples.trans: The wife is a big fan of yours, you will sit and joke with them.

examples.text: Посидишь и пошутишь — это уже называется корпоратив!
examples.trans: Sitting and joking—that is called a corporate gig!

examples.text: Я смотрю, вы легковерный! Я же пошутила!
examples.trans: I see you're gullible! I was only joking!

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'this, it (is)', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Да, это факт, место здесь очень уютное.
examples.trans: Yes, that is a fact, the place here is very cozy.

examples.text: Простите, в этом городе сквозняки страшнее цен.
examples.trans: Excuse me, in this city drafts are scarier than prices.

examples.text: Подождите, это ещё что такое во дворе?
examples.trans: Wait a minute, what on earth is that in the courtyard?

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian conversational adverb meaning 'already', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Здравствуй, Саша! Я уже могу тебя поздравить?
examples.trans: Hello, Sasha! May I congratulate you already?

examples.text: Посидишь и пошутишь — это уже называется корпоратив!
examples.trans: Sitting and joking—that is called a corporate gig!

examples.text: Ресторан ты мне уже продал.
examples.trans: You already sold the restaurant to me.

meanings.note: Prefix 'на-' marks surface contact, accumulation, or completing a quantity (stem 'зываться'). Reflexive/intransitive verb with the postfix '-ся'/'-сь' (historically from the reflexive pronoun 'себя', oneself). Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'is called'.

examples.text: Как называется этот город?
examples.trans: What's this town called?

examples.text: Операция называется Золотой ярд.
examples.trans: The operation is called Golden Yard.

examples.text: Товарищ генерал, операция называется Золотой ярд.
examples.trans: Comrade General, the operation is called Golden Yard.

meanings.note: Common masculine noun meaning 'corporate gig / party' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: Посидишь и пошутишь — это уже называется корпоратив!
examples.trans: Sitting and joking—that is called a corporate gig!

examples.text: На кухне ресторана всегда есть корпоратив.
examples.trans: In the restaurant kitchen there is always corporate gig.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian conversational adverb meaning 'almost, nearly', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Дима, что это с тобой? Ты чуть не заплакал?
examples.trans: Dima, what is wrong with you? Did you almost cry?

examples.text: Я чуть не упал.
examples.trans: I nearly fell.

examples.text: Подожди чуть-чуть.
examples.trans: Wait a little.

meanings.note: Prefix 'за-' marks beginning an action, covering, or stopping by along the way (stem 'плакать'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'started crying'.

examples.text: Дима, что это с тобой? Ты чуть не заплакал?
examples.trans: Dima, what is wrong with you? Did you almost cry?

examples.text: Надо всё сделать и заплакать вовремя.
examples.trans: We need to do everything and started crying on time.
